meta.title: File Upload
meta.description: A complete file upload system with drag-and-drop, per-file progress tracking, cancel support, error recovery, and grid/list views. Bring your own upload function — the system handles everything else.

blocks.content: File upload is the most state-heavy primitive in most apps. Each file is its own state machine: idle → queued → uploading → done or error. The user needs to cancel mid-upload. Retry a failed one. Remove a completed one. The UI has to reflect all of it simultaneously, per file.

The engine owns all of that state. You supply one function — onUpload — and the system handles the rest: drag-and-drop via react-dropzone, per-file progress bars, cancellation via AbortController, error recovery with retry, and view mode switching between grid and list. Your function calls onProgress(0–100) as bytes move. Everything else is wired.

blocks.title: The engine never uploads
blocks.content: onUpload is always provided by you. The system manages state, progress, and error recovery — it has no knowledge of your backend. This makes it compatible with any upload target: S3 presigned URLs, Cloudinary, your own API, or a mock function in development.
Drop any files below. Upload progress is simulated. Name a file starting with "fail" to trigger the error state.

blocks.label: Interactive demo

blocks.content: The simplest usage is FileUploadRoot with your onUpload function. The system renders a dropzone, progress list, and upload button automatically.

blocks.title: The engine never uploads
blocks.content: onUpload is always provided by you. The system never knows how to upload — it only manages state, progress, and error recovery. This makes it compatible with any backend: S3, Cloudinary, your own API.
Pass a config prop to restrict file types, size, and count. The dropzone automatically shows these constraints as hints.

blocks.code:
<FileUploadRoot
  config={{
    accept: { "image/*": [".jpg", ".png", ".webp"] },
    maxSize: 5 * 1024 * 1024,   // 5MB in bytes
    maxFiles: 5,
    multiple: true,
    title: "Upload product images",
    description: "JPG, PNG, or WebP up to 5MB",
  }}
  onUpload={...}
/>

blocks.content: Call onProgress(pct) with a number 0–100 as the file uploads. XHR gives you this for free via the upload progress event.
Build your own UI from scratch using useFileUpload. The hook gives you access to all upload state and actions — addFiles, removeFile, retryFile, cancelFile, and uploadAll.
Use useFileUpload anywhere inside FileUploadRoot to build your own UI on top of the engine.
